summary: Under OWNER-CHALLENGE-DESIGN-01, the photonic coupler (#345) is repaired and becomes a DEVELOPMENT test Challenge. The campaign's relative-phase flips were a mode-sign ambiguity: with each port's mode normalized and signed by construction, a mirror-symmetric pair's supermode phases cancel and arg(S41/S31) = -pi/2 exactly. The reference is declared as a local-supermode model, never relabelled as the planned 3D FDTD: Carbon's own full-vector FDFD mode solver (exact on slabs, the 500 x 220 nm strip at 2.4496) tabulates the even and odd supermodes on a 41-gap ladder at 10 nm, committed and pinned by hash to the sources that built them, and a case's cross power and unwrapped common phase follow by integration in about 0.1 s. Builds are bitwise reproducible. The 12-case pilot ran 12 of 12 OK; refinement to 5 nm moves the phase difference 0.25 % and the common phase 0.024 rad, against closed-form (effective index) errors of 1.1 to 1.7 in the unit-free S-parameter score. Public TRAIN (1,000) and PRACTICE (200) pools and a 500-case private pool under an operator-held root are generated; every gate holds on all 1,700 references; on the private pool the closed-form baseline scores 1.446 and a learned Chebyshev ridge 5.8e-4. Agreement with the campaign's FDTD is supported at the 5 to 10 % level only, and for this symmetric family the reference is the conventional design method, so it is a phase-aware test Challenge, not a demonstration of engineering value. Readiness record v4 waits in CHALLENGE-READINESS-RELAY-01. Every value is a provisional DEVELOPMENT value; the registry entry stays RESERVED until the miner path (CHALLENGE-PHOTONIC-02); no qualification, reward or LIVE authority.
